entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.question: In Genesis 12:4, Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Observe that Abram sets out already old, trusting the promise.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: The text gives his age: seventy-five years old when Abram left Haran.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the end of Genesis 12:4: Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.question: In Genesis 12:5, tap the name of Abram's wife.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Identify who goes with Abram when he sets out.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: Sarai, his wife, goes with Abram toward the promised land.

feedbackWrong.a: Lot goes too, but he is the son of Abram's brother, not his wife.
feedbackWrong.b: Haran is the city they leave from, not a person.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.hint: Look for who the verse calls his wife.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.question: According to Genesis 12:1, what does the Lord tell Abram to leave?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Observe what the call costs Abram.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: The Lord asks Abram to leave his land, his relatives, and his father's house.

feedbackWrong.a: Sarai and Lot go with Abram (Gen 12:4–5).
feedbackWrong.b: The verse does not mention flocks or servants; it speaks of land and family.
feedbackWrong.c: His possessions go with him (Gen 12:5); what stays behind is the land and his father's family.

options.a: His wife and his nephew Lot
options.c: Only the city of Haran and his possessions
options.d: His land, his relatives, and his father's house

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.question: Put Genesis 12:2 together in the order of the text.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Recognize the sequence of the promises in Genesis 12:2.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: That is the verse's order: nation, name, and finally being a blessing.

feedbackWrong.default: The verse begins with the great nation and ends with Abram being a blessing.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.hint: The verse ends with an exclamation.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.question: In Genesis 12:5, to what land did Abram and his household set out?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Remember the destination of Abram's journey.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: They head for Canaan, the land the Lord was going to show Abram.

feedbackWrong.a: Egypt is not the destination here; they leave Haran for another land.
feedbackWrong.c: Shechem is a place within the land, which Abram passes through later (Gen 12:6).

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.hint: See the end of the verse.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.question: What does Genesis 12:1 say that connects to this context?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Connect Abram's departure to the Lord's call.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: The departure does not come from Abram's own plan: it is the Lord who calls.

feedbackWrong.a: The idea is not Abram's; the verse begins with the Lord speaking.
feedbackWrong.b: The text does not speak of an enemy; it speaks of a command from the Lord.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-03-.hint: See who is speaking at the start of the verse.

options.c: The Lord calls Abram to leave

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.question: In Genesis 12:2, Abram is blessed so that he himself may become a blessing.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Understand the purpose of the blessing given to Abram.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: The blessing does not stop with Abram: he receives it to pass it on.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the end of Genesis 12:2: besides being blessed, Abram "será uma bênção".

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.question: In Genesis 12:4, tap the word that links Abram's departure to the Lord's command.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Recognize the marker that links the command to obedience.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: "Portanto" shows that the departure is a response to the Lord's word.

feedbackWrong.a: "Contava" introduces Abram's age, not the link to the command.
feedbackWrong.b: "Acompanhou" speaks of Lot going along, not of the reason for leaving.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.hint: Look for a word between commas, right at the start.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.question: How does Genesis 12:3 relate to the blessing promised in 12:2?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Understand the reach of the blessing promised to Abram.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: What begins in Abram spreads out: in him all the families of the earth will be blessed.

feedbackWrong.a: The verse goes beyond Abram's family: it speaks of all the families of the earth.
feedbackWrong.b: The curse is for whoever curses; the verse ends in blessing for everyone.
feedbackWrong.d: The land is the theme of 12:1; 12:3 speaks of who will be blessed.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.hint: Compare who is blessed in 12:2 and at the end of 12:3.

options.a: It limits the blessing to Abram's family
options.b: It trades the blessing for a threat against enemies
options.c: It widens Abram's blessing to all peoples
options.d: It repeats the promise of land in other words

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.question: How does the promise unfold in Genesis 12:2–3?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Understand how the promise widens from Abram to everyone.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: The promise grows: one nation, those who join themselves to it, and at last all families.

feedbackWrong.default: The promise goes from smaller to greater: it begins with Abram and ends with all peoples.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.hint: The end point is the widest reach of the blessing.

options.c: Whoever blesses Abram will be blessed

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.question: In Genesis 12:1, what is the Lord's first command to Abram?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Remember the action that opens Abram's story.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: The new story begins with a call to leave the familiar and trust.

feedbackWrong.b: The Lord does not ask Abram to stay and take care of things; he asks him to leave his land.
feedbackWrong.c: There is no danger to flee from; it is a call from the Lord.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.hint: It is the action that puts Abram on the road.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.question: What links Genesis 12:2 to Genesis 11:4?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Relate the promise to Abram to the project at Babel.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: At Babel, they want to make a name on their own; Abram's name is given by God.

feedbackWrong.b: Abram does not seek fame: the one who makes his name great is the Lord.
feedbackWrong.c: It is the opposite of Babel: there the name is a human achievement, here a gift from God.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-03-.hint: Compare who makes the name great in each text.

options.b: Both seek fame on their own

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.question: Genesis 12:1–2 shows that Abram was chosen because he was already more faithful than others.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Interpret Abram's choosing as God's initiative, not merit.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: The text says nothing of merit: the initiative is the Lord's, who calls and promises first.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread 12:1–2: nothing is said about Abram's virtues; it all begins with the Lord speaking.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.hint: See who takes the initiative at the start of the passage.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.question: In Genesis 12:3, tap the phrase that shows the promise is not only for Abram.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Support from the text that the promise reaches all peoples.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: The promise aims at the whole world: all the families of the earth.

feedbackWrong.b: "Abençoarei" speaks of those who bless Abram; the reach appears at the end.
feedbackWrong.c: "Amaldiçoarei" protects Abram; it does not show who receives the blessing.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.hint: Look for who will be blessed at the end of the verse.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.question: What reading does Genesis 12:2–3 support about Abram's choosing?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Choose the reading the text supports about the purpose of the choosing.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: God chooses one to reach all: Abram's blessing has the world as its goal.

feedbackWrong.a: The text says that in him all the families of the earth will be blessed.
feedbackWrong.b: The text says nothing of merit; the initiative is the Lord's.
feedbackWrong.d: Choosing Abram is the way to reach the other peoples, not to leave them behind.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.hint: See where the blessing goes at the end of the passage.

options.a: The blessing was only for Abram and his descendants
options.b: Abram was chosen for being better than others
options.c: Abram is chosen to be a blessing to all peoples
options.d: God gives up on the other peoples and keeps only one

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.question: Which sequence shows the promise to Abram being fulfilled in the Bible?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: See in Abram the beginning of God's plan for all peoples.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: The promise (Gen 12:3) runs through Jesus, son of Abraham (Matt 1:1), to all nations (Rev 7:9).

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the Bible: the promise to Abram, Jesus as his descendant, and all peoples at the end.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.hint: Follow the order of the Bible: Genesis, the Gospels, Revelation.

options.a: Jesus is born as a son of Abraham
options.b: A multitude from every nation worships before the throne
options.c: God promises to bless all families in Abram

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.question: In Genesis 12:2, what will Abram become for others?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries the meaning of the promise.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: The word that runs through the passage: Abram is blessed and becomes a blessing.

feedbackWrong.a: The nation comes at the start of the verse; the end says what Abram will be for others.
feedbackWrong.b: The text does not speak of glory for Abram; it speaks of the good that reaches others through him.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.hint: It is the word that repeats in the passage, in several forms.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.question: What links Genesis 12:3 to Galatians 3:8?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.learningObjective: Connect the promise to Abram with how the NT reads it.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.feedbackCorrect: Paul reads Genesis 12:3 as good news in advance: God would bless the nations by faith.

feedbackWrong.a: When he quotes the promise, Paul speaks of gospel and faith, not law.
feedbackWrong.b: Paul quotes the promise precisely to show that it includes all peoples.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-03-.hint: See what Paul says Scripture announced beforehand.

estudo:entrada-biblia-03.context: After the fall, the story only grows darker: Cain kills his brother, the flood comes, and at Babel the peoples are scattered. In Genesis 12, the Lord speaks to a man living in Haran, Abram, and calls him to leave.
estudo:entrada-biblia-03.focusQuestion: What step of trust might God be asking of you before he shows you the whole way?
estudo:entrada-biblia-03.keywordGloss: The commitment the Lord makes to Abram: from him will come a blessing for all the families of the earth.
facts: The Lord tells Abram to leave his land, his relatives, and his father's house.
The Lord promises to make Abram a great nation.
In Abram, all the families of the earth will be blessed.
Abram set out as the Lord had commanded.
Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
They set out for the land of Canaan and arrived there.
